summary.headline: Q1 FY27 revenue rose 12% to INR486 crore and EBITDA reached INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton), with PAT at INR41 crore.
summary.overview: Sales volume was 59,000 tons, up 6.5% YoY, with revenue up 12% on higher volumes and OEM price revisions tied to input cost increases. EBITDA was INR68 crore (INR10,760/ton, management says excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds, the figure is near INR10,700/ton), and PAT was INR41 crore versus INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore a year ago. Management said demand exceeds what it can supply, the 3 lakh ton licensed capacity is the binding constraint, and it has applied for an increase to 3.6 lakh tons. Forging project with Aichi Steel is tracking on schedule with capex now below the INR475 crore estimate, and the greenfield 5 lakh ton plant scope and cost are being revised upward.

financial_highlights.value: INR10,760/ton (INR10,700 excluding treasury income from Aichi surplus funds)

financial_highlights.change: vs INR34 crore in Q4 FY26 and INR20 crore in Q1 FY26

segments.name: Automotive steel (core)
segments.commentary: Volumes were good and prices were revised upward on cost pass-through; Q1 settlement is complete with some OEMs and pending with others, where the price is expected to rise further. Maruti is about 10% of business.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Direct exports are about 6-7% of sales and indirect exports via the Aichi trading arm about 5%; management guides total exports to 7-8% (max about 10%), with Aichi roughly 40-50% of exports.

segments.name: Non-automotive / die steel (planned)
segments.commentary: Ingot casting is due in Q3 FY27 and to stabilise in Q4; die steel production is expected to be regular in FY28. Die steel imports into India are about INR1,000 crore a year, and die steel sells at about INR2.5 lakh/ton (non-ESR) versus average realisation of about INR85,000/ton.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target about 255,000 tons; FY28 target above 270,000 tons, rising to about 290,000 tons if the environmental approval for 3.6 lakh tons comes through, and 330,000-340,000 tons in FY28-29 with new capex.
EBITDA/ton range is INR8,000-11,000 currently; management intends to move to INR8,000-12,000 for next year and to INR9,000-12,000 after the new solar plant and value-added products ramp up (FY28-29).
Q2 FY27 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase request; Q3 is expected broadly flat to slightly up or down depending on raw material prices.
Rolling mill has reached 3 lakh tons input capacity and is expected to reach 330,000 tons of input, about 10% higher, within the current licence constraint.
Forging project with Aichi Steel: commissioning by Q4 FY28, with 6-12 months to fill; revenue from around end FY29 to FY30; capex below INR475 crore estimate (more than 10% saving).

New greenfield steel plant (about 5 lakh tons, to be enlarged): commissioning on track for FY29-30; land and machinery to be finalised by mid-September 2026; cost likely a little higher than earlier per ton due to metals inflation and rupee depreciation.
capex_capacity: Existing licensed capacity is 3 lakh tons; application for 3.6 lakh tons (360,000 tons melting) is pending with the Environment Ministry, with approval expected in about 3-4 months but not assured.
New reheating furnace has stabilised; new NDT (testing) line and new peeling line to be commissioned September-October 2026 to remove bottlenecks and reduce job work.
Solar: about 50% capacity addition planned in roughly 1-1.5 years; savings will be lower than phase one because local cell manufacturing rules raise panel cost.

Greenfield plant being reconfigured (scrap preheating, extra continuous testing and automatic testing lines), so capacity and cost will rise; a refined project is due at the next Board meeting, with details in next quarter.
Funding: internal cash is in hand; a capital raise is planned in FY28 with commitments from Vardhman Group and Aichi; Punjab government support is assured.
demand_pricing: Demand is strong and the company is turning away orders; there are no long-term orders, all business is repeat, and customer volumes drive supply.
Next volume lift comes from commercial production for import substitution for Maruti, expected from Q4 FY27.
Tie-ups with Aichi and Toyota Kirloskar (TKM) support approvals; TKM's new Aurangabad plant needs green steel, where the company claims to be the only Indian player with the approvals.
Price revisions follow raw material cost changes; OEMs can reverse or move prices, and the company operates within a band.
Non-auto product mix is a planned margin lever; die steel is high-price, low-volume and carries higher heat-treatment cost.

qa_highlights.question: How much of revenue is from exports, and how is business concentrated by customer?
qa_highlights.answer: Direct exports are about 6-7% and indirect exports via Aichi's trading arm about 5%; Maruti is about 10% of sales, and management says there is no concentration risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the 3 lakh to 3.6 lakh ton expansion and the 5 lakh ton greenfield plant?
qa_highlights.answer: The EC application is filed and approval is expected in 3-4 months; the greenfield land and machinery are to be finalised by August end to mid-September, and the plant will be larger than 5 lakh tons with cost likely a little higher.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the EBITDA/ton range rising from INR8,000-11,000 to INR8,000-12,000?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cites higher volumes spreading fixed costs, lower operating costs, reduced job work from Q3 FY27, and the new solar plant; the range floor is to move to 9,000 after the solar addition.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 volume target and what drives growth beyond the licence limit?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 target is about 255,000 tons, FY28 above 270,000 tons; growth beyond that needs the EC approval and new capex, and non-auto products (ingot casting, die steel, railway axles, windmill shafts) are the next growth levers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the Aichi forging project cost and timeline on track?
qa_highlights.answer: The project is on schedule for commissioning by Q4 FY28, cost is more than 10% below the INR475 crore estimate, and revenue begins around end FY29 with a 6-12 month fill-up period.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a partner for the advanced metals / aerospace JV?
qa_highlights.answer: No partner is selected; management is talking to several parties, the JV will be a separate company that is not Aichi, and it is expected to take a couple of years, so the numbers are outside the forecast horizon.

qa_highlights.question: What is the order book and realisation outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: The company has no formal order book and says it is fully booked; Q2 realisations are expected to be higher than Q1 after a 1 July price increase, while Q3 is expected broadly flat.

risks_watch: Licence cap at 3 lakh tons constrains volume; the 3.6 lakh ton EC approval is pending and not assured.
Pending OEM price settlements for Q1 and Q2 realisations depend on OEM acceptance and raw material costs.
Greenfield project cost is rising (metals inflation, rupee depreciation, added testing lines), and the refined project and cost are due in the next Board meeting and next quarter.
Solar savings in the next phase will be lower because of local cell rules, which affects the planned EBITDA/ton uplift.
The reported EBITDA of INR68 crore includes treasury income from surplus Aichi funds; management excluded it to get INR10,700/ton, so the operating figure should be tracked separately.
Direct export share was over-estimated earlier; the company will start estimating indirect component exports from next quarter.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the Aichi forging project, with clear timelines and cost savings; more cautious and hedged on the EC approval, greenfield plant cost, and pricing, which management repeatedly says will happen "when it happens".
